swell_window.source_text: The Rock switches on with swells out of the SSE to SW (157 to 225 degrees).

https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.access_and_facilities: Park at Zippers or near the Cabo Surf Hotel and walk the beach. The cliff above the break makes it easy to scout conditions before paddling out. Hazards are the main story here: shallow, sharp reef at every stage of the tide, with exposed rocks that have drawn blood from distracted surfers. Booties are worth considering. Water quality is clean.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.hazard_summary: Shallow and exposed sharp rocks.. Reef booties are common kit.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.editorial_summary: A punchy right-hand reef break sitting half a mile down the beach from the more famous Zippers, The Rock earns its name from the boulder-strewn lineup that makes every session a dodging exercise. S and SW swells in the 4-8ft range are the sweet spot, paired with W-NW winds and a mid-to-high tide to cover the shallower sections. The takeoff zone is compact, sitting right next to the namesake rock, so the peak fills fast and patience runs thin. Bottom: rock and reef. Season: April through October. Consistency: moderate, best on strong S swells. At low tide, boils and exposed sections will test your board-reading ability and your quiver, so time your sessions carefully and bring a board you don't mind dinging. Intermediate to advanced surfers only. The shallow, sharp reef is unforgiving, and this is not a break to learn on.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.skill_suitability: The Rock is a reef bottom, short punchy right-hand reef break, break suited for intermediate through advanced surfers.

coordinate.map_source: Mapbox satellite hero on SurfTrips editorial page

https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.access_and_facilities: Multiple sand parking areas line the beach. Lock your car and hide everything, petty theft is common and corrupt police have been reported in the area. Camping is available nearby. Water quality is a genuine hazard: significant raw sewage input from multiple sources makes post-rain sessions a bad idea.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.editorial_summary: Rosarito's beachbreak delivers year-round surf for a wide range of skills, sitting about 30km south of Tijuana on Baja California's north coast. Short-period NW windswells and combo SW-plus-NW setups are the sweet spot, ideally with an E wind holding up the faces. The beach faces directly west, which means anything overhead-plus on a pure swell tends to close out fast, but mid-size days from chest-high to a couple feet overhead keep things fun. Beginners can find mellow reform sections while intermediates work the pier-influenced sandbars. Bottom: sand. Season: year-round. Consistency: high. Avoid surfing here within 72 hours of heavy rain, raw sewage levels spike sharply across multiple drainage points.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.skill_suitability: Rosarito Beach is a beach bottom, west-facing beach peaks, pier-influenced sandbars, combo-swell dependent, break suited for beginner through advanced surfers. Beginners can give it a go on the smaller end of the size range.

https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.title: Monuments

coordinate.map_source: Mapbox satellite hero on SurfTrips editorial page

swell_window.source_text: Monuments switches on with swells out of the S to W (180 to 270 degrees).

https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.access_and_facilities: Drive east from Cabo San Lucas toward San Jose del Cabo. Access runs through a guarded hotel gate, security typically allows surfers through. Park above the break and take the dirt trail down. After a session, the hotel above the break serves cold beers with a direct view of the arch. Water quality is clean.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.hazard_summary: There's a big rock right in the path of the wave -- beware.. Reef booties are common kit.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.editorial_summary: A deepwater canyon just offshore funnels long-interval W and SW swells into steep, spinning lefts that reel along the headland into a small rocky bay at the southern tip of Baja. SSW, SW, and W swells are the bread and butter, with that submarine canyon amplifying long-period energy so Monuments can be double-overhead while nearby Costa Azul sits barely head-high on the same swell. NE wind is ideal, afternoon W winds regularly blow it out, so dawn patrol pays. Mid to high tide keeps the shallow rock-and-urchin bottom honest. Best from April through October. Consistent enough for intermediate surfers but the tight takeoff, powerful sets, and hazardous inside section demand focus. Crowds are moderate given proximity to Cabo San Lucas, but weekdays you may have it nearly to yourself. Bottom: shallow rocks and urchins. Season: April-October. Consistency: regional classic. Bring a step-up if the swell is running solid double-overhead, and under no circumstances put your feet down on the inside.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.skill_suitability: Monuments is a reef bottom, powerful spinning left-hand reef point, break suited for intermediate through advanced surfers.

coordinate.map_source: Mapbox satellite hero on SurfTrips editorial page

swell_window.source_text: Las Gaviotas switches on with swells out of the S to WNW (180 to 292 degrees).

https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.access_and_facilities: The break sits inside a gated condo development near K-38, closer to K-41 and K-51. Access by car is possible but requires either renting or owning a unit in the complex, or arriving with someone who does. Water quality is fair with occasional sewage spill risk, so check conditions after heavy rains. No public restrooms or rental shops on-site. Pack water, wax, and anything else you need before the gate.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.hazard_summary: Rocks, urchins, rip currents for beginners.. Reef booties are common kit.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.editorial_summary: A soft righthand reef break south of K-38 on Baja's northern coast, Las Gaviotas trades performance for accessibility, making it one of the more forgiving reef setups in the region. S and SW swells are the engine here, with W and WNW filling in when summer and autumn groundswells push up the coast. Offshore winds run NE through SE, and the wave works on all tides, which keeps sessions flexible. The reef is flat and rocky, producing mellow, rolling rights that longboarders and beginners can work without committing to a heavy paddle-out. Waist-high to overhead is the sweet spot. Crowds sit at a moderate level on weekends but thin out midweek, and the local vibe is genuinely welcoming rather than territorial. Bottom: flat rocky reef. Season: summer and autumn south swells. Consistency: moderate. Access runs through a gated condo community, so sorting that out before you arrive saves a wasted drive.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.skill_suitability: Las Gaviotas is a reef bottom, soft righthand reef break, mellow rolling walls, break suited for beginner through intermediate surfers. Beginners can give it a go on the smaller end of the size range.

tide_guidance.source_text: Offshore winds run NE through SE, and the wave works on all tides, which keeps sessions flexible.

swell_window.source_text: Quatro Casas switches on with swells out of the SE to NW (135 to 315 degrees).

https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.access_and_facilities: Off Baja 1, roughly between Colonet and Camalu. Dirt roads lead to the bluffs above the break. A 4WD is not required in dry conditions. Camping on the bluffs is popular and a small fee applies. Theft has been reported at isolated camp spots, so camp near others. Pack all trash out. Water quality is clean.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.hazard_summary: Turning your back to the ocean..
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.editorial_summary: A sheltered right-hand reef and semi-point tucked along the Baja 1 corridor, Quatro Casas is a SoCal favorite that punches well above its modest reputation. It catches south swell reliably in summer and lights up on clean NW pulses through winter, with the bluffs and kelp bed killing most wind chop. NE offshores are ideal. Best from head-high to double overhead, though a veteran local notes it starts closing out past 11-12ft. The wave is organized and forgiving enough for beginners but has enough shape to keep shortboarders interested. Weekdays are quiet, weekends bring moderate crowds drawn by easy Baja access. Bottom: Rock reef/point. Season: March-October best, rideable year-round. Consistency: High for the region. Bring a variety of boards and arrive early on weekends, the lineup fills quickly and the fun-wave format means everyone wants in.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.skill_suitability: Quatro Casas is a point bottom, fun walling right-hand reef/point, organized and wind-sheltered, break suited for beginner through advanced surfers. Beginners can give it a go on the smaller end of the size range.

https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.access_and_facilities: The road in is rough and requires a capable vehicle. No formal parking area exists, so high-clearance four-wheel drive is the practical choice. Camping is available on-site. Bring all supplies: water, food, fuel, and spares. No shops or medical facilities are nearby.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.editorial_summary: A hollow right-hand point north of Punta Rosalillita, Puerto San Andres punches above its size when strong W swell lines up with the powerful NE offshores that define this stretch of Baja's mid-peninsula coast. Optimal conditions call for a solid W to NW swell in the 2-8ft range, light NE winds, and the point works across all tides, giving it a longer usable window than many neighboring breaks. Consistency is medium, so timing matters: the spot fires most reliably during the winter NW swell season when groundswells push down the Pacific coast. Intermediate surfers will find the most reward here, and crowds are only occasional given the rough road access. Bottom: point. Season: Oct-Mar. Consistency: medium. Pack food, water, and camping gear as facilities are limited to a basic campsite and the nearest services are a rough drive away.

https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.access_and_facilities: No road access. Boat charter from Puerto San Carlos is the only way in. Bring all food, water, sunscreen, and spare leashes. Water temp runs warm enough for boardies or a light 1mm through summer, spring and fall mornings may call for a 2mm top. Watch for rocks near Cuevas at lower tides.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.editorial_summary: Two right-hand points and a right reef called Cuevas sit inside Magdalena Bay on Baja Sur's Pacific coast, reachable only by boat out of Puerto San Carlos. The setup fires on S to SW swells from spring through fall, with offshore winds keeping faces clean across a size range of roughly 3 to 8ft. Mid-tide tends to be the sweet spot on the points, while Cuevas can handle a bit more water. Intermediate surfers will find plenty to work with, and the boat-only access filters the crowd down to almost no one on most days. Bottom: mixed reef and point. Season: April through October. Consistency: moderate, swell-dependent. Pack everything you need before leaving San Carlos, because there are no facilities once you're out on the water.

https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.access_and_facilities: Follow La Bocana / Punta China signs south of Ensenada. A 4WD or high-clearance vehicle is strongly recommended. Free camping is available on-site with basic facilities. Bring all food and water from Ensenada before heading down the dirt access road.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.editorial_summary: A south-facing point on the Baja coast below Ensenada, Boca De Santo Tomas combines a right-hand pointbreak with rocky beachbreak and a rivermouth, all tucked behind enough headland to stay glassy when northerly winds are howling. It works best on S to NW swell in the 3-10ft range, with the kelp helping to hold the surface smooth and the south-facing orientation providing solid wind protection most days. Optimum tide is all tides, though the point's longer walls favor mid-incoming when push starts organizing the sets. Intermediate surfers get the most out of the varied setups here, and crowds are manageable outside of busy holiday weekends when Ensenada day-trippers make the drive. Bottom: point and rocky beach. Season: late summer through early winter for combined S and NW groundswells. Consistency: medium. Follow signs for La Bocana and bring a 4WD or high-clearance vehicle because the dirt access trail can get rough after rain.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.skill_suitability: Boca De Santo Tomas is a mixed bottom, wind-protected right-hand point with rocky beach and rivermouth sections, break suited for intermediate surfers.

https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.access_and_facilities: Drive-up access with parking directly at the break. No significant hike required. The area has food and water options nearby. Water quality is clean. Sand and rock bottom means the risk of a hard wipeout is present, so booties are worth considering if you are surfing the shallower inside section.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.editorial_summary: A mellow right-hander on the Pacific coast of Baja California Sur, Old Man's rolls through like a small reef pass, offering forgiving walls that suit a wide range of ability levels. It works best on SSE to SSW swell, mid tide, with N or NW winds pushing offshore to clean up the face. Size sweet spot is knee-high to overhead. The crowd is consistently heavy year-round, but the vibe stays welcoming since the lineup skews toward beginners and longboarders rather than territorial locals. Bottom: sand and rock. Season: April to October. Consistency: reliable through the warmer months. The main hazard is other surfers, not the ocean itself, so stay aware of who is paddling around you, especially on bigger sets when less experienced riders lose control of their boards.

https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.title: Marisol North Point

coordinate.map_source: Mapbox satellite hero on SurfTrips editorial page

swell_window.source_text: Marisol North Point switches on with swells out of the N to E (0 to 90 degrees).

https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.access_and_facilities: A parking lot faces the break directly, street parking is available when the lot fills. Being near the main public beach means basic amenities are close, but this is Lake Michigan in winter: pack warm layers, hot drinks, and dry bags. The current risk on south-wind days is serious, if swept around the point, ride the current shoreward, exit the water, and re-paddle from further down the beach.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.editorial_summary: A ledgey left-hand barrel peeling over shallow rock on the northern shore of Lake Michigan, Marisol North Point is one of the only spots on the Great Lakes capable of breaking boards on a solid day. NW to NE fetch drives the best swells, and the wave works across all tides, though a strong south wind triggers a nasty rip that drags surfers around the point fast. Suited to experienced surfers only: drops are late, fast, and close to vertical over a rock ledge sitting roughly three feet deep. Crowds are essentially non-existent on weekdays and weekends alike, but good days are rare. Bottom: rocky reef. Season: late fall through winter, when Great Lakes fetch peaks. Consistency: low to moderate, working days measured in weeks per year, not months. Bring a helmet and booties, the ledge is unforgiving and the water is cold year-round.
https://surftrips.co/mexico/baja-califor.skill_suitability: Marisol North Point is a reef bottom, short hollow ledging left-hand barrel, break suited for advanced surfers. This is not a beginner break. Build up at softer waves first.

tide_guidance.source_text: NW to NE fetch drives the best swells, and the wave works across all tides, though a strong south wind triggers a nasty rip that drags surfers around the point fast.
